exposure: Timing of CHIKV infection (during pregnancy vs. outside of pregnancy vs. no infection)
outcome: Pregnancy complications (abruption, vaginal bleeding, preterm labor/cervical incompetence, cesarean delivery for fetal distress/abruption/placental abnormality, delivery for fetal distress)
cohort: 731 mother-infant pairs who gave birth during a Chikungunya outbreak in Grenada between January 2014 and September 2015.
finding: CHIKV infection during pregnancy did not appear to pose a risk for pregnancy complications or neonatal health, but maternal infection just prior to delivery might have increased risk of mother-to-child transmission of CHIKV.
